name: Discovery Park of America
unique: A hundred thousand square foot museum and heritage park built by a local foundation in a town of eleven thousand, with a full dinosaur hall, a cave replica, a 100 foot tower you can climb and a recreated 1800s settlement outdoors.
buzz: The scale does not make sense until you walk in. Families plan whole days, and the tower view over the delta farmland is the surprise ending.

name: Reelfoot Lake North Shore
dates: Year round, best winter for eagles
unique: The northern end of a lake formed by the 1811 New Madrid earthquakes, where cypress trees stand in the water and the shallows hold more wintering eagles than almost anywhere in the lower forty eight.
buzz: The cypress in fog is the photograph. Hunters and anglers know the north end as the quiet side of the lake.

name: Union City Downtown Square
unique: A courthouse square in the middle of the flat farmland of the Obion basin, with a landmark obelisk on the lawn and a block of shops that still serves the surrounding cotton and soybean country.
buzz: The square is where you eat before or after Discovery Park. Nothing fancy and everything works.

name: Reelfoot Lake State Park
cost: Free, camping and boat rental extra
unique: A state park on a shallow natural lake that formed when the ground sank during the 1811 and 1812 earthquakes, with cypress stumps, a boardwalk, boat ramps and a visitor center that explains the geology and the birds.
buzz: The boardwalk through the cypress is the easy win and the lake is best in winter when the eagles come down. Locals fish for crappie and bluegill all spring.

name: Reelfoot Eagle Eye Van Tour
dates: January and February, seven days a week
unique: Ranger driven van tours that run all winter to the places bald eagles concentrate on the lake, with spotting scopes and a ranger who knows which tree the nest is in.
buzz: Tickets are cheap and the tours fill in January. People see dozens of eagles in two hours and the rangers call out what to look for.

name: Reelfoot Lake Boardwalk and Spillway
unique: A raised walkway out into the cypress shallows where you look down into the water at gar, turtles and the flooded stumps of a forest that drowned two centuries ago.
buzz: The best short stop on the lake and it is free. Early morning light through the cypress is what photographers come for.

name: Shiloh National Military Park
customer: Civil War people, families, history travellers
unique: The battlefield where the bloodiest engagement of the war to that point was fought in April 1862, with the sunken road, the peach orchard, earthworks, a national cemetery and more than twenty miles of driving tour.
buzz: Rangers and historians call it the best preserved and best interpreted battlefield in the west. The Hornet's Nest and the cemetery are what people remember.

name: Pickwick Landing State Park
unique: Fourteen hundred acres on the Tennessee River below Pickwick Dam, with an inn, cabins, a marina, a golf course and some of the best bass and sauger water in the state.
buzz: The inn is a cheap base for the lake and the tailwater below the dam fishes all winter. Summer weekends the marina is full.

name: Cherry Mansion
unique: An 1830s house on the bluff above the Tennessee River where Grant kept his headquarters before Shiloh and where he was sitting when the first reports of the battle arrived.
buzz: The river view from the porch explains why Grant chose it. Tours are by arrangement and the volunteer knows the details.

name: Savannah Historic District
unique: A river town grid of antebellum and Victorian houses above the Tennessee, with a main street that ran on river freight before the railroad moved the trade away.
buzz: Quiet and unpolished, with more original houses than most towns this size. The bluff walk over the river is the highlight.

name: Sheriff Buford Pusser Home and Museum
customer: Film fans, true crime people, families
unique: The actual house where the McNairy County sheriff lived, kept as it was when he died in 1974, with the car, the guns and the case files from the bootlegging war that inspired the Walking Tall films.
buzz: The house is a time capsule and the volunteers who run it grew up with the story. Some visitors find it a shrine and others a warning, and the museum lets both sit there.

name: Big Hill Pond State Park
unique: Nearly five thousand acres of bottomland forest and bluff along the Hatchie River, with a raised boardwalk across a cypress swamp, a fire tower and horse trails through some of the best remaining hardwood bottomland in the state.
buzz: The boardwalk and the fire tower are the easy highlights and the birding in spring migration is exceptional. Rarely crowded, even on holidays.

name: Selmer Courthouse Square
unique: A small county seat square in the loess hills of southwest Tennessee, with the courthouse, a monument and the shops that serve a county of twenty five thousand.
buzz: A useful stop between Shiloh and the Hatchie bottoms. The diners around the square are the reason to get out of the car.

name: Eiffel Tower Park
unique: A scale replica of the Eiffel Tower in a public park in a Tennessee town called Paris, with a fountain, a walking track and a sign that makes the joke for you.
buzz: It is sixty feet of steel lattice and everybody photographs it. The park around it is where the town walks in the evening.

name: World's Biggest Fish Fry
company: City of Paris / Paris-Henry County Chamber
unique: The 73rd edition of a nine day catfish festival that serves tens of thousands of pounds of fish from a permanent fry shed, with a parade, a rodeo, a carnival and a midway.
buzz: It is genuinely enormous for a town this size and the fish is the point. Locals take the week off to work the fry.

name: Paris Landing State Park
unique: Eight hundred acres on the widest part of Kentucky Lake, with an inn, a marina, a golf course and a fishing pier where the crappie run in spring.
buzz: The lake view from the inn rooms is the selling point and the spring crappie fishing draws boats from three states.

name: Paris Downtown Square
unique: A courthouse square of 1890s buildings with a fish market, a bakery and a department store that has never left, in the town that calls itself the capital of Kentucky Lake.
buzz: The square is intact and the food is the draw. During the fish fry it is the center of everything.

name: Pinson Mounds State Archaeological Park
unique: The largest Middle Woodland mound complex in the southeast, with Sauls Mound rising seventy two feet, a geometric earthwork enclosure and a museum holding the artifacts and the unresolved questions about who built it.
buzz: You can climb the big mound and see the whole layout. The museum is small and the site is quiet, which makes the scale of the earthworks hit harder.

name: Casey Jones Village
unique: The house where the locomotive engineer Casey Jones lived, moved to a village beside the tracks with a railroad museum, a caboose, a general store and a restaurant that has fed interstate traffic for decades.
buzz: The museum tells the 1900 wreck and the ballad that made him famous, and the trains still run past the door. A good stop with kids on a long drive.

name: International Rock-A-Billy Hall of Fame
unique: A fan built museum and hall of fame for rockabilly in the town where Carl Perkins recorded for Sun, packed with stage clothes, guitars, posters and a stage that still hosts shows.
buzz: Run by believers rather than a corporation, which shows in the collection and in the hours. Ask about the Saturday shows.

name: Jackson Depot and Downtown
unique: A restored railroad depot and a downtown grid that grew on the Mobile and Ohio line, with the old courthouse, a farmers market and the bones of a cotton and rail city.
buzz: Downtown Jackson has filled back in with restaurants and a market. The depot is the anchor and the architecture is worth the walk.
